messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

Given the following text and a relational triplet extracted from it:

Text: Hydroxyzine hydrochloride (HCl) and hydroxyzine pamoate are two salt forms of the same active medicine.
Taken by mouth, FDA-approved labeling gives them the same approved uses.
It gives them the same doses.
It gives them the same warnings.
It gives them the same side effects.
The injection is the exception.
It is a hydroxyzine HCl product.
There is no pamoate injection.
It has its own approved uses, doses, and warnings.
The practical differences are:
Form.
Hydroxyzine hydrochloride comes as tablets and as an oral solution.
Hydroxyzine pamoate comes as capsules.
How they dissolve.
Hydroxyzine hydrochloride is very soluble in water.
Hydroxyzine pamoate is practically insoluble in water.
How the strength is measured.
Hydroxyzine pamoate capsules are labeled by the amount of hydroxyzine HCl they are equivalent to.
A 25 mg pamoate capsule delivers the same amount of active medicine as a hydroxyzine hydrochloride 25 mg tablet.
The two salts also had different brand names.
Vistaril was the brand name for hydroxyzine pamoate.
Atarax was the brand name for hydroxyzine hydrochloride.
Triplet: ["Hydroxyzine hydrochloride", "has same warnings as", "Hydroxyzine pamoate"]

The relation 'has same warnings as' in the triplet is defined as 'The subject drug has the same safety warnings or precautions as the object drug.' In this context, is there any relation appropriate to replace it? Choose a relation whose meaning and subject/object direction match the triplet even if the wording differs; choose 'None of the above' only if no candidate fits. Please answer by providing only the letter of your choice.

B. 'reduces risk of': The subject drug is used to prevent or lower the risk of the medical event or condition specified by the object entity.
C. 'has rules on': The subject drug is subject to the rules specified by the object entity.
D. 'similar to': The subject drug is related to or an alternative for the drug specified by the object entity.
